newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian share trade dull, RTF slips.
newsitem.headline: Latvian share trade dull, RTF slips.

text.p: Trade on the Latvian stock market remained quiet on Thursday although overall volumes were a touch higher than yesterday with Riga Transport Fleet falling and Valmiera Glassfibre rising.

Trade was 86,000 lats versus Wednesday's 73,000 lats. The most active share was leading bank Unibanka, which lost one santime to 3.78 lats on turnover of 20,600 lats. The Rietumu Bank index slipped 0.67 percent to 193.52.
"One of the reaons for the quiet market could be that some funds have left it as people prepare for the big privatisations where vouchers are needed," Hansabank-Latvija dealer Andreta Petersone said.
She said that trade may recover once the shares of Riga Shipyard hit the market, expected soon as it held its auction for cash earlier this week.
RTF was the biggest faller among leading shares, losing 6.5 percent to 1.43 lats on 8,000 lats trade.
Rietumu Bank dealer Dmitry Krutik said in his daily stock market bulletin that the fall was due to the blocking of shares ahead of the April 26 shareholder meeting.
RTF also earlier told Reuters that its first quarter results would be close to the planned levels although it did not reveal any figures.
Valmiera Glassfibre rose to 1.75 lats from 1.68 lats on trade of 6,500 lats.

Company officials earlier said they expected first quarter profits of around 200,000 lats versus 600,000 lats in the first quarter of 1996. They said the fall was due to a falling German mark as many of their sales are in Germany.
Daugavpils Chain was active on trade of 18,800 lats and fell slightly to 2.68 lats from 2.70 lats.
Kaija lost two santimes to 2.54 lats and traded 10,800 lats of shares.
